account: Contributor 01 joined a project initiated by Contributor 04 to replace a pre-existing conductivity-assay worksheet that accepted impossible dilution combinations. During 1 April–31 May, Contributor 01 mapped the existing rules while explicitly deferring unresolved assay-policy decisions; wrote the validation layer and inline errors; sought bench-workflow review; moved a warning earlier and added a disposal-case test after feedback; detected a mixed-unit defect during the pilot, stopped release, and prepared the correction; and implemented bounded migration exception handling for verified aliases. Assay requirements remained Contributor 03’s responsibility, the broader workflow came from Contributor 04’s process map, and Contributor 02 supplied key bench feedback. The release was controlled and limited to the pilot laboratory, not organisation-wide adoption. Afterwards, a blank result was released despite the configured supervisor-signoff control. Contributor 01 proposed both a mandatory reason and a more visible blank warning, then implemented the narrower approved change: foregrounding the blank flag and adding acknowledgement. Reviewers explicitly warned that this improved salience but did not prove appropriate supervisor decisions. Full-record evidence also indicated later quality review and postponed expansion, but the quantitative outcome and expansion claims are not included below because their citation-span identifiers were not retained in the surfaced tool output. Research stopped at the 45-call source limit with six surfaced records and two attachments unread.

claims.limits: The evidence identifies the immediate pre-project problem and collaborators, not the worksheet’s original author or how long the defect had existed.
